titleEn: Say Sorry, Let Your Heart Shine!

pages.text: Playing toss-it-high—"Oops!" Dari's throw sent Kongal's rattle against the bedroom wall. Two shells tied with string; now one was cracked. Dari stopped dead.
Kongal cried in the cradle. Dari held a shell in his mouth. He should say he had done it, but his mouth stayed shut. He slid the rattle under the quilt.
Mom came upstairs and picked Kongal up. "Why crying? Where's the rattle?" "...Don't know." Dari turned away and fiddled with the quilt's edge.
Mom looked at his face. "Your heart feels heavy?" She settled him on her lap and patted him. "It's okay. What could help?" Dari thought quietly.
Dari lay on the quilt, pressing his chest. Keeping quiet felt like fog inside it—tight and prickly. "How do I clear this fog?"
Kongal reached a little flipper toward him from the cradle. "Aah, aah." Kongal wanted to play with Dari. His heart thumped. The baby had reached first.
Dari took the rattle from under the quilt, breathed deeply, and held it out. "Mom, I threw it and broke it. Kongal... I'm sorry!" Mom stroked his back. "Say sorry, let your heart shine!"
The heart-fog cleared, bright as the lighthouse lamp. Mom brought another shell. Dari tied the string tightly. Rattle, rattle! A new rattle lay beside the cracked one.
Dari set the new rattle before Kongal. Giggles! Dari slapped his tail. Now he knew what to do after breaking something. "One, say 'I did it.' Two, say sorry. Three, fix it together!"
Mom hugged both children. "Wonderful to know how to say sorry!" Hiding mistakes filled his heart with fog; speaking made it bright again. Say sorry, let your heart shine!
